Name: Bananthimari Betta
Summary: A quick, rocky climb close to Bangalore: rock steps, boulders and big views, back home by lunch.
Description: A short morning trek up a rocky hill near Kanakapura, about 60–70 km from Bangalore. The trail starts at the Bananthimari temple at the base and climbs rock steps, then a boulder section, to the summit: about 5 km round trip. The hill is in a reserve forest where elephants move after dark, so we start at first light, not in the dark.
BestSeason: September – February (best); year-round with an early start
Itinerary:
5:00 AM
Depart from Bangalore.

6:30 AM
Reach the temple at the base. Safety briefing and start the climb at first light.

8:00 AM
Reach the summit. Time for photos and snacks.

9:30 AM
Descend and have breakfast.

12:00 PM
Arrive in Bangalore.
Inclusions:
Return transport from Bangalore (for Bangalore pickups)
Breakfast after the trek
Entry fees, if any
Experienced trek lead and first-aid kit

Name: Bandaje Falls
Summary: Evergreen forest, open grassland ridges and the top of the Bandaje Arbi falls.
Description: A full-day trek from Valambra near Ujire, through evergreen forest and open grassland ridges, to the top of the Bandaje Arbi falls in the Kudremukh National Park area. About 14–16 km round trip. Trails can close at short notice in the fire season. Permits are booked on the Forest Department's Aranya Vihaara portal, and a certified forest guide is mandatory.
Itinerary:
Night before · 10:00 PM
Depart from Bangalore. Overnight drive to the base village.

Day 1 · 6:00 AM

Day 1 · 7:00 AM
Start the trek from Valambra. Hike through evergreen forest and open grassland ridges.

Day 1 · Midday
Reach the top of the Bandaje Arbi falls. Packed lunch with a view.

Day 1 · Evening
Back at the base. Start the drive home, reaching Bangalore late at night.
Inclusions:
Return transport from Bangalore (for Bangalore pickups)

Forest permits and entry fees

Name: Huttari Betta (Hutridurga)
Summary: A short climb through the gateways of Kempegowda's hill fort to a boulder-topped summit.
Description: Hutridurga (Uttari Betta), about 65–75 km from Bangalore. A 5–6 km round trip up stone steps, through the gateways of Kempegowda's 16th-century hill fort, to a boulder-topped summit with the Shankareshwara temple and views over lakes and farmland.

Name: Kudremukh
Summary: Rolling green hills, streams and the famous horse-face peak inside Kudremukh National Park.
Description: Kudremukh (1,894 m) is the "horse-face" peak inside Kudremukh National Park. The trail starts at the forest checkpost at Mullodi near Kalasa: about 22 km round trip through shola forest and rolling grasslands, with several stream crossings. A long but steady day. Permits are booked on the Forest Department's Aranya Vihaara portal, and a certified forest guide is mandatory.

Name: Kumara Parvatha
Summary: One of Karnataka's toughest treks: dense forest, steep grassland and a summit above the clouds.
Description: Kumara Parvatha (Pushpagiri, 1,712 m) in Kodagu. For the 2026 season the Forest Department has opened the Beedahalli route, about 14 km round trip with long, steep sections, so good fitness is a must. It is a day trek only: camping on the mountain is not allowed. The Kukke Subramanya route has not reopened yet. Permits are booked on the Forest Department's Aranya Vihaara portal, and a certified forest guide is mandatory.

Description: Netravati Peak (about 1,520 m) from Samse village near Kalasa: about 12 km round trip through forest and open grassland, with a steeper final stretch. Slots sell out fast. Permits are booked on the Forest Department's Aranya Vihaara portal, and a certified forest guide is mandatory.

Name: Skandagiri Sunrise Trek
Summary: A pre-dawn climb with the official sunrise slot, often above a sea of clouds.
Description: Starts behind the Papagni Mutt in Kalavara village, Chikkaballapur, about 65–70 km (around 1.5 hours) from Bangalore. About 8 km round trip to the summit. Entry is only with a slot booked in advance on the Forest Department's Aranya Vihaara portal, which we do for you: the sunrise slot reports at the base gate around 3:30–4:00 AM, late arrivals are turned away, and unbooked night treks are not allowed. On winter mornings the summit is often above a sea of clouds.

Name: Tadiandamol
Summary: Coorg's highest peak: shola patches, grassy slopes and an open summit.
Description: Tadiandamol (1,748 m) is the highest peak in Coorg. The trail starts at the Nalknad Palace near Kakkabe: about 14 km round trip through shola patches and grassy slopes to an open summit. Day trek only (no camping), and the forest checkpoint closes in the afternoon, so we start early. Permits are booked on the Forest Department's Aranya Vihaara portal, and a certified forest guide is mandatory.
